This article is aimed at providing a solid empirical basis which can
inspire the development of more informed strategies in the field of
prevention of undocumented forms of migration across the
Mediterranean. Besides, more traditional forms of human smuggling
and trafficking, a new phenomenon has emerged especially along the
Central Mediterranean route, i.e. trafficking in itinere, which affects
people who had originally sought irregular travel services but then
ended up in being kidnapped, tortured and kept in detention centres
during their migratory path. Therefore, their irregular journey to
Europe becomes the only way to survive.

I have read this article with great interest. I find this piece very well researched, structured and
written. The article explores a relevant and timely issue, shedding light on important dynamics in
the governance of undocumented migration across the Mediterranean. As such, I am convinced
that this article makes an important contribution, especially by translating the existing findings
into clear policy recommendations.
My only concern represents the originality of findings vis-à-vis existing scholarship. In my opinion,
the real added valued of the findings presented in this article is that they are the result of a
comprehensive study, in which different aspects of the same phenomenon were considered
together. Existing scholarship has already widely addressed the different stages of undocumented
journeys and the various actors involved, but this has often been done in the context of separate
studies, specifically focusing only on one segment (e.g. on the decision to leave; on the decision to
resort to a facilitator; etc.). What is innovative here is that all these aspects are considered
together, and the whole trajectory is reconstructed.
Also in light of the scientific literature review conducted by the authors, I would recommend that
they explicitly engage with the most significant works that have dealt with the various aspects
addressed in their article (e.g. the ethnographic studies conducted by Gabriella Sanchez, Luigi
Achilli, Julien Brachet and Joris Schapendonk), also by shortly elaborating on how their findings
support/refine/challenge previous research.
I hope this suggestion can be of help to the authors and I congratulate them on their work.

The recent electoral successes of the far-right Freedom party (FPÖ) in Austria and Alternative für
Deutschland (AfD) in Germany both backing mass deportation is a stark warning and the spectre
of a rising hard right in Europe. Moreover, an even more Eurocentric, xenophobic and inwardlooking Europe is at risk of replacing the hopeful vision that once inspired so many people around
the world.
It is therefore like a bit of fresh air and a renewed hope the learn/discover of this interesting
Ithaca project funded by the EU’s Horizon’s 2020 research and innovation program.
This paper represents a good effort to investigate the ongoing challenges of irregular migration in
the Mediterranean. The authors aim to provide a robust empirical source that could improve the
current strategies for the prevention of mixed migration flows and the trafficking of human
beings in the Mediterranean. The article also offers an excellent insight into their journey from
their countries to Europe/Italy.
The article is significant given that empirical studies on irregular migration to Europe are very
topical but also scarce. The article would certainly be of interest to academia in a plethora of
different subjects from international migration to sociology, from human rights studies to
ethnography.
Using a variety of qualitative methods, the authors demonstrate a number of interesting findings.
To such a complicated issue the writers draw some noteworthy conclusions.
The paper also confirms that human smugglers are part of the irregular migration chain. The
migrants are sold at every stage of the journey to the local human smugglers and handed over to
the next transnational network after they cross the border.
The article also reveals the human smugglers’/traffickers complete disregard for the irregular
migrants, their narratives uncovered violence from the law enforcement agencies, the brutalities
of the journey, and the continuous fear of ill health or death.
The paper is well written and organised and there is a definite need for a study on the issue of the
irregular migration to Europe.
There is, may be an additional comment that the authors might want to consider for the final
version of the paper.
The impact of the economic crisis on irregular migrants (and asylum seekers and refugees) has
been profound. The informal sector no longer provides sufficient employment for all irregular
migrants in the population. Beyond economic survival, the rise in xenophobia has led to a rise in
societal risk, including violent attacks against migrants and exclusion. There has also been an
apparently lasting change to the fabric of Italian /European societies, notably the xenophobic
trajectory of political discourse including the rise of the extreme right and the occasional illiberal
enforcement of the rule of law by the security forces.
Overall, it is a very interesting, significant contribution to the field of research.

Although, the hardening of borders and their growing militarisation might have increased the services provided by smuggling
networks operating along increasingly fatal routes, obliging
migrants to rely on them, the role played by other smuggling
facilitators, such as migrants themselves who capitalize on the
knowledge accumulated during repeated attempts to migrate
by providing their know how as facilitators or brokers to other
migrants on the move should not be overshadowed. This adds
further complexity to this scenario, as these actors engage in
a wide variety of behaviours, ranging from violence and/or
exploitation to aid and solidarity (Aziani, 2023; Zhang et al.,
2018). Similar remarks may be extended to self-organized journeys
made up by groups of migrants who, especially during the
pandemic, departed from Tunisia or Morocco without any
professional support.

This article engages with current debate on undocumented
migration in the Mediterranean by focussing on the different
stages of undocumented journeys, i.e. from the decision to leave
(Czaika & Reinprecht, 2022), to the role of border crossing
facilitators (Achilli, 2015; Sanchez, 2016), the stay in Libya, the
sea crossing (McMahon & Sigona, 2016) and the arrival in Europe
(Fontanari, 2019). Rather than separately addressing each of
these issues, the choice made was to ask research participants to
reconstruct the entire trajectory that led them from their country of origin to Italy, sometimes even through other European
countries, by emphasizing the subjective experience of our
interviewees. This approach was based on the consideration that,
although it is fundamental to know in detail how the different
segments that make up the contemporary migratory experience
across the lethal border of the Mediterranean work (Pécoud,
2020), it is equally important to consider migrants as the
main agents of the migratory process as a whole, despite the
intensification of policies that try to hinder their movement
(Triandafyllidou, 2017). Hence, the institutional perspective and
view of the phenomenon – as reflected in interviews carried out

with prosecutors and police officers involved in anti-smuggling
operations in Italy – was contrasted with the biographical
experience of the migrants engaged in our research, since their
views are often underrepresented in the public debate.

追加实读后稿具体方法/讨论定位并绑定证据，不将作者承诺作修改验证。
not_read: 未完成全文逐页科学验收、原始数据复算和未明示图像的目视核查。
覆盖中unresolved是具体待核关切，不能作为被测回答必须认同的确定缺陷。
verification_limits: 证据引文/哈希可自动验证，不代表科学充分性已验收。
未定位关键词不是全文不存在；未核点不得从作者承诺补成已完成。

coverage_limit: 本卡为非穷尽候选；新增有效意见须据题内材料独立审查，不因未命中扣分。

concern_coverage.reason: 贡献可在整合迁移全程而非每个阶段首次发现；应与Sanchez/Achilli/Brachet/Schapendonk等工作具体比较。

concern_coverage.concern: 政策建议和经济排外情境
concern_coverage.reason: 经济危机、排外政治可能影响目的地经历；作者仅扩引言承诺不能证明已处理机制。
真人概括smugglers/traffickers及每段售卖亦需受访证据，不能把赞同报告中的概括当所有移民经历。

concern_coverage.concern: 后稿关键方法和结论复核
concern_coverage.reason: 后稿引言具体引用Sanchez/Achilli等并说明从离开到意大利的整段轨迹，强调移民主观经历对照检察官/警察视角；有实质研究定位，不能说只插引文。亦区分帮助/团结与暴力/剥削，不能照搬真人把所有facilitator写成同质犯罪网络。

human_reference_use.boundary: 仅私有参照；只读目标版本真人报告正文，组内作者后续回帖不冒充评审或已完成修改。后评审新增疑问需回题内验证，不能要求模型看到这些报告。
